title: Fix How It Acts, Not How It Thinks: Surgical Fine-Tuning of Frontier LLMs
read_level: partial (arXiv HTML v1: abstract, Secs 1-3 incl. vanishing-delta analysis and Table 1, Sec 6 results, Sec 7.1, related work, Sec 9 limitations, Appendix E compute; other appendices and Secs 4-5, 7.2-7.5 not read in full)
why_wsp: Gradient-based LoRA fine-tuning (merge-aware, straight-through gradient through rounding) of Nemotron-3.5 120B; no LLM editor, and the paper does not cite or position itself relative to weight-space programming.
exclusion_reason: Gradient-based LoRA fine-tuning with no LLM editor; no citation of or positioning relative to WSP (no Takehi et al. or 'weight-space programming' reference found).
target: NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5 120B, BF16 release and mixed FP8/NVFP4 release (attention q,k,v,o; Mamba in_proj; shared experts)
interface: other (LoRA adapter trained with straight-through gradient through Q_fmt rounding)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "Fewer than 3% of the adapted weights deviate from the base weights, and all others remain bit-identical." (Sec 6); "only 2.6% of elements are updated by at least half an ulp" (Sec 2); rho = 3.1e-5 relative served change.

headline_results.quote: In our BF16 release, the median weight change is only 1.5% of a single rounding step, and merging loses roughly two thirds of the update's norm.
When the same adapter is merged into the mixed FP8/NVFP4 release of the same model, 93% of the update disappears.
93% of the update is lost, and the shared-expert weights, which are stored in 4 bits, do not change at all.
the surviving update only has a cosine similarity of about 0.26 to the direction of the update that was learned during training
The BF16 loss is consistent over all the module groups (at 63 - 68%) ... the FP8 groups only retain 8 - 12% of the update norm, and the 4-bit experts do not retain any.

headline_results.where: Table 1 (update norm / served change / retained kappa / lost)

headline_results.claim: Rounding threshold for a BF16 weight
headline_results.quote: An update must reach the midpoint to a neighboring value to avoid being rounded away, which requires a change of about 0.2 - 0.4% of the weight's magnitude.
for FP8 in the E4M3 format ... the grid is 16x coarser than BF16 for similar magnitudes. And NVFP4 is much coarser, with only seven nonzero magnitudes
If we merge the BF16 adapter at step 5 and step 10 ... only 7% and 9% of the update norm survive ... at the released checkpoint (step 100) 34% ... and at the end of training (step 158) 38%.
cosine similarities of W'-W with the trained update sBA of only 0.24 - 0.28 across the BF16 module groups, and 0.11 - 0.14 in the FP8 groups of the NVFP4 release

headline_results.claim: Standard LoRA control loses gain after merge
headline_results.quote: On Terminal-Bench 2.1 it gets a score of 63.5, vs. 69.1 for our release and 60.7 for the base.

headline_results.claim: Standard LoRA merge retains same share
headline_results.quote: they preserve almost the same fraction of the update (kappa=0.343 vs. 0.341), have the same cosine similarity ... (0.26 each)
The biggest improvement is on Terminal-Bench 2.1, with 69.1 vs. NVIDIA's reported 60.7.

cost.quote: The BF16 run took 2.94 hours on 8 B300 GPUs, including startup and checkpoint saves.
The NVFP4 run took 5.1 hours on 4 B300 GPUs

baselines_and_controls: Base BF16 and NVFP4 models (NVIDIA-reported and own harness); standard LoRA with same data/objective merged by plain rounding; checkpoints at different steps.
runs_and_variance: "We average the SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench scores over 2 to 6 runs. DeepSWE and NL2Repo-Bench use a single run" (Sec 5).
robustness_of_edits: Core topic: small weight updates largely vanish under BF16 rounding (about 66% of norm lost) and FP8/NVFP4 merging (93% lost; 4-bit experts unchanged). Relevant to persistence of small WSP-style edits through release formats.
verification: none formal; merge validation and export checks (Appendix B, not read in full)
limitations_stated: Full benchmark suite not run on unreleased checkpoints; only standard LoRA compared, not stochastic rounding or other retention methods; effect specific to small updates and coarse formats.
notes_for_survey: Out of scope as WSP, but its measurements bear on edit persistence: sub-ulp weight changes are rounded away when stored in BF16, and FP8/NVFP4 storage removes most or all of a small update. A WSP edit expressed as small deltas would need to be checked in the served number format.
